The dependencies and optional dependencies listed are appropriate for an Electron-based application like Tropy that handles image and PDF processing. There are no signs of obfuscated commands, unauthorized network requests, or suspicious operations in this file. While the use of mutable git sources inherently carries a supply-chain risk (as the checked-out commit could change), this is a standard practice for `-git` AUR packages and not a sign of malicious intent. The actual security of the build depends on the integrity of the upstream repository and the included `tropy.sh` script, but this file alone does not introduce any malicious behavior.

It clones the upstream source from the official GitHub repository (`https://github.com/tropy/tropy`), applies necessary patches for integration with the system (such as using the system Electron and adjusting paths), and builds the package using npm and electron-packager. All operations occur within the build environment, and no external or untrusted code is downloaded during the build process.

The use of `sha256sums=('SKIP')` is expected and appropriate for VCS sources like git, as the content is inherently mutable and checksums cannot be pinned. The `prepare()` and `build()` functions modify package.json and internal scripts to ensure compatibility with Arch Linux's filesystem layout and packaging policies, which is normal for AUR packages.

There are no signs of obfuscated code, unauthorized network requests, data exfiltration, or execution of unsanctioned payloads. All modifications are transparent, well-documented in the script, and aligned with the goal of integrating Tropy into the system securely and reproducibly. The package installs only into standard system directories under `$pkgdir`, and post-install actions are limited to desktop integration (icons, MIME types, metadata), which are standard.
</details>
